dossier.purpose: Docker Compose v5 is a Go command-line tool that reads Compose-spec files (via compose-spec/compose-go v2, go.mod:11) and builds/pulls images, then creates, starts, stops and removes the containers, networks and volumes of a multi-service application on a Docker Engine API endpoint. Every resource is tagged with com.docker.compose.* labels so a project can be found again (pkg/api/labels.go:25-70). It ships as a Docker CLI plugin (`docker compose`), as a standalone `docker-compose` binary (cmd/main.go:37-86), and as an importable Go SDK (github.com/docker/compose/v5/pkg/api and pkg/compose; docs/sdk.md). It contains no container runtime of its own: it needs a reachable Docker Engine (local socket or a Docker context) and, for BuildKit builds, the buildx plugin (pkg/compose/build_bake.go:55-74).

claims.claim: Docker Compose is a tool for running multi-container applications on Docker defined using the Compose file format (compose-spec.io).
A Compose file is used to define how one or more containers that make up your application are configured.
Once you have a Compose file, you can create and start your application with a single command: `docker compose up`.

Quick start is a three-step process: (1) define the app's environment with a Dockerfile 'so it can be reproduced anywhere'; (2) define the services in compose.yaml 'so they can be run together in an isolated environment'; (3) run `docker compose up` and Compose 'will start and run your entire app'.
Example Compose file: a `web` service (build: ., ports 5000:5000, bind volume .:/code) plus a `redis` service from image redis.
Docker Compose is included in Docker Desktop for Windows and macOS.

Linux: download Docker Compose binaries from the GitHub release page, rename the relevant binary to `docker-compose` and copy it to $HOME/.docker/cli-plugins, or into one of four system-wide cli-plugins directories (/usr/local/lib|libexec/docker/cli-plugins, /usr/lib|libexec/docker/cli-plugins); may need `chmod +x`.
Docker Swarm relied on the legacy compose file format, did not adopt the Compose specification, and after acquisition by Mirantis is not maintained by Docker Inc.
The Python version of Compose is available under the `v1` branch.
Badges: GitHub release, pkg.go.dev docs for github.com/docker/compose/v5, CI status, Codecov, OpenSSF Scorecard.
Contributions and bug reports go through CONTRIBUTING.md and the GitHub issue tracker.

install.command: No command: install Docker Desktop, which bundles Compose (https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/).

install.method: Linux, per-user: release binary as Docker CLI plugin
install.command: Download the binary for your OS/arch from https://github.com/docker/compose/releases, rename it to `docker-compose`, copy it to `$HOME/.docker/cli-plugins`, and `chmod +x` if needed (README gives this as prose; no literal shell command is given).

install.method: Linux, system-wide: release binary as Docker CLI plugin
install.command: Copy the renamed `docker-compose` binary into one of: `/usr/local/lib/docker/cli-plugins` OR `/usr/local/libexec/docker/cli-plugins`; `/usr/lib/docker/cli-plugins` OR `/usr/libexec/docker/cli-plugins`.

install.method: Build from source (BUILDING.md lists Linux, macOS and Windows prerequisites: Docker, make, Go per go.mod)
Build and install as CLI plugin from source (Makefile target; not described in README or BUILDING.md)
install.command: make install   (runs `docker buildx bake binary`, then copies the binary to ~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - README documents Linux release binaries (README.md:40-52); release matrix includes linux/amd64 (docker-bake.hcl:121) published as docker-compose-linux-x86_64 (Dockerfile:204-214); CI e2e runs on ubuntu-latest against Docker Engine 29 and 28 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:167-201).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no mention of WSL or WSL2 in README, docs, Go code, Makefile, Dockerfile or workflows (case-insensitive search returned no matches). A Linux binary would be the relevant artifact, but WSL2 is neither documented nor tested.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - release matrix includes darwin/arm64 (docker-bake.hcl:117-118); darwin is cross-built with osxcross, CGO and the `fsnotify` build tag (Dockerfile:30-31, 104-107); README says Compose is included in Docker Desktop for macOS (README.md:36-38). CI build, unit-test and e2e jobs run only on Linux runners (ci.yml:26, 140, 168), so darwin binaries are cross-compiled but not executed in CI.
platforms.gpu: yes (pass-through only) - `gpus:` and deploy.resources.reservations.devices are translated into engine DeviceRequests, and CDI device names use driver 'cdi' (pkg/compose/create.go:768-798, 835-843). Availability depends on the host engine/runtime, which Compose does not install or check; no GPU tests exist (search of *_test.go for gpu/nvidia/DeviceRequest: no matches).

integrations.cli: yes - Docker CLI plugin `docker compose` (cmd/main.go:37-79, plugin.Run with metadata Vendor 'Docker Inc.') and standalone `docker-compose` (cmd/main.go:81-86; flag translation in cmd/compatibility/convert.go:55-108); CI tests both modes (ci.yml:176-191). 35 documented subcommands (docs/reference/compose.md:11-49) plus hidden `alpha` and `hooks` (cmd/compose/alpha.go:26; cmd/compose/hooks.go:164). Machine-readable output: `--progress json` (cmd/compose/compose.go:722-725, 769-775) and `version --format json` (cmd/compose/version.go:64-66).
integrations.mcp: none found - case-insensitive search of Go, Markdown, YAML, JSON, HCL and go.mod for 'MCP' / 'Model Context Protocol' returned no matches. (The `docker model` plugin used for `models:` in pkg/compose/model.go:81-105 is the Docker Model Runner, not MCP.)
integrations.sdk_or_api: Go SDK, no HTTP/daemon API. Module github.com/docker/compose/v5 (go.mod:1); the `api.Compose` interface (pkg/api/api.go:94-165) is obtained with `compose.NewComposeService(dockerCli, opts...)` (pkg/compose/compose.go:65), documented in docs/sdk.md:1-162; the doc's Go snippets are checked against compiled examples by docs/examples/sdk/sdk_md_test.go:28-57. docs/sdk.md contains no API-stability statement. Also an inbound extension protocol: `provider:` services run an external binary implementing `compose up|down|stop|metadata` and speaking JSON lines on stdout (docs/extension.md:13-61, 142-215; pkg/compose/plugins.go:42-61, 192-208).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: none found as a product integration - no CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .codex/ or .mcp.json. Contributor-facing only: AGENTS.md:1-60 gives AI coding agents build/test/lint/DCO sign-off rules and requires an AI_AGENT_DISCLOSURE.md file on agent-prepared PRs (AGENTS.md:44-60), enforced by .github/workflows/ai-disclosure-gate.yml:16-25; CI also runs an AI PR-review action (.github/workflows/pr-review.yml:21).

readme.telemetry_and_network: README is silent on telemetry, network requirements and accounts (README.md read in full). Code/docs findings: (1) TELEMETRY: no analytics, usage-ping or update-check code found (case-insensitive search of all Go files for analytics|segment|telemetry|phone home|check for update matched only OpenTelemetry imports). OpenTelemetry tracing is initialised on every plugin command (cmd/main.go:54-56; cmd/cmdtrace/cmd_span.go:49-68) but exports only if (a) any OTEL_*ENDPOINT environment variable is set, giving an OTLP/gRPC client (internal/tracing/tracing.go:121-143), or (b) the active Docker context metadata has an `otel` entry with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (Docker Desktop path), dialled only over a unix socket or named pipe (internal/tracing/docker_context.go:37-77, 81-113; internal/memnet/conn.go:26-34). With neither, the exporter list is empty (internal/tracing/tracing.go:66-110) and no spans leave the process. When enabled, spans carry project name/dir/compose-file paths, volume/network/secret/config names, service names and images, container ids/names, a project hash (internal/tracing/attributes.go:66-160) and CLI flag names (not values) (cmd/cmdtrace/cmd_span.go:60-63). No dedicated opt-out variable exists (search for DO_NOT_TRACK / COMPOSE telemetry switches found none). (2) REQUIRED NETWORK SERVICES: only a Docker Engine API endpoint (local socket by default; remote engines via Docker context/host handled by docker/cli; standalone mode forwards --host/--context/--tls* in cmd/compatibility/convert.go:44-53). Image pulls/pushes go through the engine to registries using credentials from the Docker CLI config (pkg/compose/pull.go:295-315; pkg/compose/push.go:94-100); default registry constants point at Docker Hub (internal/registry/registry.go:28-41). (3) OPTIONAL OUTBOUND FETCHES: git remotes via the local `git` binary (pkg/remote/git.go:172-228) and `oci://` Compose artifacts via containerd's resolver with Docker CLI credentials (pkg/remote/oci.go:116-186; internal/oci/resolver.go:45-75). Both are enabled by default (pkg/remote/git.go:41-52; pkg/remote/oci.go:73-82) and the CLI has no offline flag (flags at cmd/compose/compose.go:224-237; Offline is set only during shell completion, cmd/compose/completion.go:42, 90). `docker compose bridge` uses transformer images such as docker/compose-bridge-kubernetes (pkg/bridge/transformers.go:32-45). (4) DOCKER DESKTOP: when the engine advertises label com.docker.desktop.address, Compose talks to Desktop over a local socket (feature flags, logs hints: internal/desktop/client.go:38-41, 143-176; cmd/compose/hooks.go:93-95) and routes OCI registry traffic through Desktop's HTTP proxy socket, deliberately ignoring the local NO_PROXY (internal/desktop/proxy.go:90-153). (5) ACCOUNTS: Compose has no account or login of its own; credentials come from the Docker CLI config and credential helpers, and `use_api_socket` copies all of them into the container (pkg/compose/apiSocket.go:48-62, 85-88). (6) LOCAL STATE WRITTEN: remote-file cache at $XDG_CACHE_HOME/docker-compose or ~/.cache/docker-compose (~/Library/Caches/docker-compose on macOS) (pkg/remote/cache.go:24-36; cache_unix.go:30-36; cache_darwin.go:28-34); provider metadata at <docker config dir>/compose/providers/<type>.json (pkg/compose/plugins.go:273-277); per-project watch pidfile lock (cmd/compose/watch.go:96-103; internal/locker/runtime_unix.go:31-43). (7) DRY RUN is not offline: it no-ops mutations but still reads real engine state and performs registry manifest lookups with real credentials (pkg/dryrun/dryrunclient.go:78-95, 234-260).

code.architecture: Single Go module producing one static binary that is both a Docker CLI plugin (`docker compose`) and a standalone `docker-compose` (CGO off except darwin: Dockerfile:48, 106). Layers: (1) cmd/ - main.go wraps docker/cli plugin.Run and, when standalone, rewrites args through cmd/compatibility; cmd/compose/*.go are the cobra commands (RootCommand registers 36: cmd/compose/compose.go:515-552) and ProjectOptions (cmd/compose/compose.go:140-418), which resolves project name, compose files (-f / COMPOSE_FILE, default compose.yaml discovery in the working dir and parents), env files (OS environment wins over --env-file/.env, compose.go:388-389) and profiles; cmd/display and cmd/formatter render progress/logs (tty|plain|json|quiet); cmd/prompt asks confirmations; cmd/cmdtrace + internal/tracing add OpenTelemetry spans. (2) pkg/api - the public `Compose` interface, option structs, `com.docker.compose.*` label constants and event types (pkg/api/api.go:94-165; labels.go:25-70). (3) pkg/compose - the implementation over the Docker Engine API client from docker/cli (pkg/compose/compose.go:65, 233-235): loader.go (compose-go load plus git/OCI remote loaders in pkg/remote); build.go + build_bake.go (shells out to `docker buildx bake`) or build_classic.go (engine ImageBuild); pull.go/push.go; create.go -> observed_state.go (label-filtered snapshot of containers/networks/volumes) -> reconcile.go (desired vs observed) -> plan.go (DAG of atomic operations, one engine call each) -> executor*.go (parallel DAG walk) (pkg/compose/create.go:68-137; plan.go:30-56; executor.go:68-120); start.go and service_containers.go (depends_on waiting at :162-222); up.go (attach, log printing, monitor.go); down.go/stop.go/remove.go/kill.go; watch.go + pkg/watch (file sync/rebuild); plugins.go (provider services); model.go (`docker model` plugin); pre_start.go/hook.go (lifecycle hooks); secrets.go (secrets/configs copied into containers); publish.go + internal/oci (publish Compose artifacts to OCI registries after a sensitive-data scan); generate.go (Compose project from existing containers). (4) Supporting: pkg/dryrun (APIClient wrapper that no-ops mutations), pkg/bridge (compose -> Kubernetes/Helm via transformer images), internal/desktop (Docker Desktop local-socket client and proxy), internal/registry (credential lookup), internal/sync (tar-based file sync), pkg/mocks (generated gomock mocks).
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: static binaries for 11 OS/arch targets (darwin amd64/arm64; linux amd64, arm/v6, arm/v7, arm64, ppc64le, riscv64, s390x; windows amd64/arm64) built with `docker buildx bake release` (docker-bake.hcl:116-137), named docker-compose-<os>-<arch>[variant][.exe] with x86_64/aarch64 arch names (Dockerfile:204-214); version injected via -ldflags -X internal.Version from `git describe` (Makefile:16-18). CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml): the `binary` job calls the reusable workflow docker/github-builder bake.yml pinned to commit a492c6d0 (v1.16.0) with sbom: true, sign: true on non-PR events and `id-token: write` for GitHub OIDC (ci.yml:48-62); `binary-finalize` renames per-binary `.provenance.json`, `.sbom.json` (SPDX) and `.sigstore.json` (Sigstore provenance bundle), writes `checksums.txt` (SHA-256) and one `<binary>.sha256` per binary (ci.yml:64-119). The `release` job, on `v*` tag pushes, uploads bin/release/* to a DRAFT GitHub release with generated notes and overwrite_files: false (ci.yml:343-380). merge.yml publishes multi-arch images docker/compose-bin (tags: git tag, edge) and docker/compose-desktop-module (pushed only on v* tags) with SBOM and OIDC attestations (merge.yml:18-79; Dockerfile:194-230). Linux distro packages are built outside this repo by docker/docker-ce-packaging using `make build DESTDIR=...` (Makefile:48-53). Signing/attestation logic lives in the external reusable workflow, whose contents were not inspected. Docs differ from code: BUILDING.md:87-95 says to 'run the release GitHub Actions workflow' and that it creates the tag, but no separate release workflow exists - releases come from ci.yml on `v*` tag pushes (ci.yml:10-15, 343-345), as a draft. No CHANGELOG file; release notes are generated by GitHub (ci.yml:375).
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: Go `testing` with gotest.tools/v3 (assert, icmd, golden files via -test.update-golden: BUILDING.md:39) and go.uber.org/mock gomock (generated mocks in pkg/mocks, regeneration validated in CI: Makefile:96-105, Dockerfile:77-94); goleak is a dependency (go.mod:52). Approx. 127 `_test.go` files with 629 top-level Test functions (regex `^func Test`): 50 files / 210 functions in pkg/e2e (build tag `e2e`, needs a live Docker daemon: BUILDING.md:45; new tests use a declarative Scenario DSL: pkg/e2e/SCENARIO.md:1-70, AGENTS.md:13-20) and 77 files / 419 functions of unit tests across cmd/, pkg/{api,bridge,compose,remote,utils,watch}, internal/ and docs/examples/sdk (mock the engine API; no daemon needed: AGENTS.md:7-8). Run via `make test` (-> `docker buildx bake test`, Dockerfile:121-132) and `make e2e-compose` / `make e2e-compose-standalone` (Makefile:78-84, 20 min timeout). Workflows (.github/workflows): ci.yml - `validate` matrix (golangci-lint v2.13.2, go.mod tidy check, license headers, docs regeneration check, mocks check: ci.yml:25-46; Dockerfile:18-21, 64-94, 110-119, 138-192), `test` (unit tests + coverage: ci.yml:139-165), `e2e` matrix of 6 (plugin and standalone x Docker Engine 29 with graphdriver and containerd image store, plus Engine 28 graphdriver) on ubuntu-latest with Docker installed from test.docker.com and docker-model-plugin (ci.yml:167-301), `coverage` merge to Codecov (ci.yml:303-341), `binary`, `bin-image-test`, `release`. Others: merge.yml (image publishing), docs-upstream.yml (validates reference YAML against docker/docs), scorecards.yml (OpenSSF Scorecard, weekly + on main), zizmor.yml (workflow static analysis, pedantic persona), ai-disclosure-gate.yml, pr-review.yml + pr-review-trigger.yml (AI PR review), stale.yml. Dependabot: gomod and github-actions daily (.github/dependabot.yml:1-38). No govulncheck/gosec/Trivy/CodeQL-analysis workflow; the golangci-lint set has no gosec (.golangci.yml:13-33).
code.dependencies: go.mod (module github.com/docker/compose/v5, go 1.26.3) + go.sum; the only module in the repo; no vendor/ directory. 54 direct requirements (go.mod:6-59), 75 indirect (go.mod:63-137), 2 excluded versions (go.mod:140-147). Core: compose-spec/compose-go/v2 v2.15.0 (:11), docker/cli v29.7.2+incompatible (:18), moby/moby/client v0.5.1 and api v1.55.0 (:32-33), moby/buildkit v0.33.0 (:30), containerd/v2 v2.3.4 (:13), spf13/cobra v1.10.2 (:42), OpenTelemetry SDK/OTLP v1.46.0 (:46-51), grpc v1.83.2 (:57), DefangLabs/secret-detector (:7, used by `publish` secret scanning), AlecAivazis/survey/v2 (:6, prompts). Test-only: gotest.tools/v3 (:58), go.uber.org/mock (:53), goleak (:52). Runtime external executables not in go.mod: `docker buildx` plugin >= 0.17.0 for the BuildKit path, `git` for git remotes, `docker model` plugin for `models:`, any provider binary.
code.security_policy: .github/SECURITY.md - report privately to security@docker.com, not as a public issue (SECURITY.md:6-9); acknowledgement within 72 hours (:11-12); draft GitHub security advisory for confirmed issues (:20-23); no paid bounty (:35-36); only the current release and `main` are maintained, Compose v1 is EOL (:38-43). CONTRIBUTING.md:28-39 repeats the private-reporting rule.

claim_checks.claim: Docker Compose is a tool for running multi-container applications on Docker defined using the Compose file format (README.md:19-20).
claim_checks.evidence: Root command is described as 'Define and run multi-container applications with Docker' (cmd/compose/compose.go:449). Files are loaded with compose-spec/compose-go v2 (go.mod:11; pkg/compose/loader.go:56) and applied to a Docker Engine through the moby API client, one engine call per plan node (pkg/compose/compose.go:233-235; pkg/compose/plan.go:30-56; pkg/compose/executor_ops.go:40-145).

claim_checks.claim: You can create and start your application with a single command, `docker compose up` (README.md:23-24).
claim_checks.evidence: `up` ensures images (build/pull), models, networks, volumes, then reconciles and executes a plan, then starts services (pkg/compose/create.go:68-137; pkg/compose/up.go:44-52; cmd/compose/up.go:113-147, 254-270), with depends_on ordering (pkg/compose/service_containers.go:162-222). It requires a reachable Docker Engine; there is no embedded runtime.

claim_checks.claim: Services defined in compose.yaml 'can be run together in an isolated environment' (README.md:61-62).
claim_checks.evidence: Isolation is by naming, labels and networks, not a sandbox. Resources carry com.docker.compose.project/service labels (pkg/api/labels.go:25-29) and are found by project-label filter (pkg/compose/filters.go:33-35); containers are named <project>-<service>-<n> (pkg/compose/service_containers.go:135-137); services join a project-scoped 'default' network (pkg/compose/create.go:640, 657-686; names like test_default in pkg/compose/executor_test.go:72); `down` removes only that project's non-external networks/volumes (pkg/compose/down.go:148-161, 206-220). Host exposure remains configurable: published ports and host bind mounts (README.md:73-75) and `use_api_socket`, which mounts the Docker socket (pkg/compose/apiSocket.go:69-73).

claim_checks.claim: A Dockerfile defines the app's environment 'so it can be reproduced anywhere' (README.md:59-60).
claim_checks.evidence: Builds go through `docker buildx bake` when BuildKit and buildx >= 0.17.0 are present, else a classic engine build without multi-arch/secrets/ssh/additional contexts (pkg/compose/build.go:99-106; pkg/compose/build_bake.go:55-74; pkg/compose/api_versions.go:65-66; pkg/compose/build_classic.go:235-247). Compose does not lock inputs by default: image tags float unless pinned; `config --resolve-image-digests` / `--lock-image-digests` can pin (cmd/compose/config.go:154-155). `up` recreates containers only on config-hash or image divergence (docs/reference/compose_up.md:15-17; pkg/compose/reconcile.go:348-352). Engine and buildx versions are environmental inputs.

claim_checks.claim: README example (build: ., ports 5000:5000, bind volume .:/code, image redis) is supported (README.md:66-78).
claim_checks.evidence: build -> pkg/compose/build.go:79-106; ports -> engine ExposedPorts/PortBindings (pkg/compose/create.go:321, 405); bind mount -> mount.BindOptions (pkg/compose/create.go:1407-1424); image pull -> pkg/compose/pull.go:295-315.

claim_checks.claim: Docker Compose is included in Docker Desktop for Windows and macOS (README.md:36-38).
claim_checks.evidence: Bundling happens in Docker Desktop and cannot be checked from this repo. The repo does build and publish a Docker Desktop module image docker/compose-desktop-module containing the plugin for darwin/windows/linux (Dockerfile:219-230; docker-bake.hcl:156-168; .github/workflows/merge.yml:56-79; desktop-module/module-metadata.json:1-9) and contains Desktop-specific code (internal/desktop/client.go:38-41; internal/desktop/proxy.go:41-54).

claim_checks.claim: Linux install: download release binary, rename to docker-compose, copy into a cli-plugins directory (README.md:42-52).
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from README in detail: release assets are named docker-compose-<os>-<arch> (Dockerfile:204-214), so the rename step is needed, and are attached to a draft GitHub release (ci.yml:343-380). Plugin lookup directories are implemented by docker/cli's plugin manager (external dependency, go.mod:18), so the four system-wide paths cannot be verified in this repo. The binary also runs standalone as `docker-compose` (cmd/main.go:81-86), which README does not mention; `make install` copies to ~/.docker/cli-plugins (Makefile:73-76).

claim_checks.claim: Docker Swarm is not maintained by Docker Inc. and lacks recent Compose syntax (README.md:26-30).
claim_checks.evidence: Statement about third-party maintenance status; no code evidence either way. Code treats Swarm only as a special case when resolving external overlay networks (pkg/compose/create.go:1516-1526; pkg/compose/compose.go:486-500).

claim_checks.claim: The Python version of Compose is available under the `v1` branch (README.md:89-92).
claim_checks.evidence: The working copy is a shallow clone containing only tag v5.5.1 (.git/packed-refs:1-3), so the v1 branch cannot be inspected. .github/SECURITY.md:40-43 states Compose v1 reached EOL and is unsupported.

claim_checks.claim: Badges: Go package docs for github.com/docker/compose/v5, CI, Codecov, OpenSSF Scorecard (README.md:12-16).
claim_checks.evidence: Module path is github.com/docker/compose/v5 (go.mod:1); ci workflow exists (.github/workflows/ci.yml:1); Codecov upload (ci.yml:338-341; codecov.yml:1-21); Scorecard workflow (.github/workflows/scorecards.yml:1-66). Badge values are served externally and are not in the repo.

risks: Scope is one Docker Engine endpoint, not a scheduler: all operations use a single engine API client chosen by the Docker CLI context (pkg/compose/compose.go:233-235; standalone mode forwards --host/--context/--tls* flags: cmd/compatibility/convert.go:44-53). README says Swarm does not use the Compose spec and is not maintained by Docker Inc. (README.md:26-30); code only special-cases Swarm when resolving external overlay networks (pkg/compose/create.go:1516-1526). No code or doc mentions Podman, nerdctl or other engines (case-insensitive search), so non-Docker engines are unaddressed.

Compatibility matrix is narrower than the build matrix and README states no minimum versions. Features are gated on negotiated Docker Engine API 1.44 / 1.48 / 1.49 (pkg/compose/api_versions.go:21-51; pkg/compose/create.go:631-634, 668, 1033-1040; pkg/compose/service_containers.go:417); BuildKit builds need buildx >= 0.17.0 (api_versions.go:63-67; build_bake.go:478-495) with a reduced-feature classic fallback (build_bake.go:64-74; build_classic.go:235-247); `models:` needs the Docker Model plugin (pkg/compose/model.go:81-88). CI runs only Linux runners and Docker Engine 28 and 29 (ci.yml:167-201); darwin, windows, arm, ppc64le, riscv64 and s390x binaries are cross-compiled but not executed in CI, WSL2 is not mentioned anywhere, and there are no GPU tests.

Credential and code-execution surface: `use_api_socket: true` bind-mounts /var/run/docker.sock into the service and writes every credential returned by the Docker CLI config into the container at /run/secrets/docker/config.json (pkg/compose/apiSocket.go:48-62, 65-90). `provider:` services run any executable resolvable as a Docker CLI plugin or on PATH, with the project environment (pkg/compose/plugins.go:192-208; pkg/compose/shellout.go:37-49), and cache provider metadata under the Docker config dir (plugins.go:273-277). Builds, git remotes and models shell out to `docker buildx`, `git` and `docker model` (pkg/compose/build_bake.go:172-182; pkg/remote/git.go:174, 200-221; pkg/compose/model.go:118).

Remote Compose sources are on by default although their toggles are named COMPOSE_EXPERIMENTAL_GIT_REMOTE / COMPOSE_EXPERIMENTAL_OCI_REMOTE (pkg/remote/git.go:41-52; pkg/remote/oci.go:42-82). The CLI has no offline flag (cmd/compose/compose.go:224-237; Offline is set only during shell completion: cmd/compose/completion.go:42, 90). Mitigation present: for a remote main file, `up`/`run` list interpolation variables and ask for confirmation unless --yes (cmd/compose/options.go:123-176, 263-290). Fetched content is cached under ~/.cache/docker-compose (pkg/remote/cache.go:24-36).

State and scope defaults to know: (a) `--yes` auto-confirms every prompt, including 'Volume ... exists but doesn't match configuration in compose file. Recreate (data will be lost)?', whose default is false (cmd/compose/up.go:284-286; pkg/compose/compose.go:184-189; pkg/compose/reconcile.go:353-396); in a non-TTY without --yes the answer comes from stdin and empty means no (cmd/prompt/prompt.go:96-102; pkg/utils/stringutils.go:25-32). (b) Without -f, Compose searches the working directory and its parents for compose.yaml/docker-compose.yaml and defaults the project name to the directory basename (docs/reference/compose.md:115-116, 181-195; cmd/compose/compose.go:407-408), which decides which labelled resources are touched (pkg/compose/filters.go:33-35). (c) `down -v` deletes non-external named volumes, while anonymous volumes are not removed by default (pkg/compose/down.go:133-135, 148-161; docs/reference/compose_down.md:12-16). (d) `--dry-run` no-ops mutations but still reads real engine state and does registry lookups with real credentials (pkg/dryrun/dryrunclient.go:78-95, 234-260).

Telemetry hook exists though inert by default: tracing is initialised on every plugin command (cmd/main.go:54-56) and, if an OTEL_*ENDPOINT variable is set, exports spans over OTLP/gRPC to that endpoint (internal/tracing/tracing.go:121-143). Spans can include project name/directory, compose file paths, service images, volume/network/secret/config names and a project hash (internal/tracing/attributes.go:66-139). Docker Desktop's context metadata can also enable export over a local socket (internal/tracing/docker_context.go:37-77). No dedicated opt-out variable exists.

Maintenance and process: only the current release and `main` are maintained, no long-term-support branches (.github/SECURITY.md:38-43). No CHANGELOG or MAINTAINERS file in the repo; release notes are generated at release time (ci.yml:375) and maintainer rules live in an external repo (CONTRIBUTING.md:254-260). Stale-issue bot closes issues 30 days after a 150-day stale mark, exempting kind/feature and kind/enhancement (.github/workflows/stale.yml:24-27). pkg/e2e/SCENARIO.md:3-4 states coding agents write most of the production code; CI runs an AI PR reviewer (pr-review.yml:21) and gates agent-prepared PRs on removal of AI_AGENT_DISCLOSURE.md (ai-disclosure-gate.yml:16-25). docs/sdk.md makes no API-stability statement.

Supply chain and licensing: test/lint tooling is fetched unpinned (`go run gotest.tools/gotestsum@latest`: Makefile:80, 84 and Dockerfile:131; `gofumpt@latest`: Makefile:131); the e2e job installs Docker by running get-docker.sh from test.docker.com (ci.yml:213-219); docs validation calls a reusable workflow at docker/docs@main (docs-upstream.yml:41); release signing/provenance is delegated to the external docker/github-builder workflow (ci.yml:49), not inspected. No workflow runs govulncheck, gosec, Trivy or CodeQL analysis, and .golangci.yml has no gosec (13-33). Licensing: repo is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE); six files embed code adapted from MIT-licensed adrg/xdg with attribution only in comments (pkg/remote/cache_darwin.go:24-25, cache_unix.go:26-27, cache_windows.go:26-27; internal/locker/runtime_darwin.go:24-25, runtime_unix.go:27-28, runtime_windows.go:26-27); NOTICE has only Docker attribution (NOTICE:1-4); there is no vendor/ or third-party license inventory, so licenses of the 54 direct dependencies (go.mod:6-59) were not audited.

checks.field: readme.install[1] (Linux, per-user: release binary as Docker CLI plugin)
checks.statement: Download the binary for your OS/arch from https://github.com/docker/compose/releases, rename it to `docker-compose`, copy it to `$HOME/.docker/cli-plugins`, and `chmod +x` if needed (README gives this as prose; no literal shell command is given).
checks.note: README.md:42-43 points to the GitHub release page. :45 says 'Rename the relevant binary for your OS to `docker-compose` and copy it to `$HOME/.docker/cli-plugins`'. :52 says it 'might require making the downloaded file executable with `chmod +x`'. The instructions are prose only, as the dossier says. The rename step matches the release asset naming docker-compose-${TARGETOS}-${TARGETARCH} (Dockerfile:212-214).

LICENSE:2-4 reads 'Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004'. The terms end with 'END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS' at :177, followed by the standard appendix at :179-202. The text is unmodified Apache-2.0. The revision was also confirmed: .git/packed-refs:2-3 peels tag v5.5.1 to 5f94fb0aa42a2cd1248c6e6c7fafb87546b9c8de, and .git/HEAD is the same commit.

checks.statement: yes - README documents Linux release binaries (README.md:40-52); release matrix includes linux/amd64 (docker-bake.hcl:121) published as docker-compose-linux-x86_64 (Dockerfile:204-214); CI e2e runs on ubuntu-latest against Docker Engine 29 and 28 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:167-201).
checks.note: README.md:40-52 is the '### Linux' install section. docker-bake.hcl:121 is "linux/amd64" in target binary-cross (:116-131), which target release inherits (:133-137). Dockerfile:212 maps amd64 to x86_64, and :214 writes docker-compose-${TARGETOS}-${TARGETARCH}${TARGETVARIANT}, which gives docker-compose-linux-x86_64. ci.yml:168 sets the e2e job to runs-on: ubuntu-latest. The matrix at :176-201 covers engine 29 (graphdriver and containerd stores) and engine 28 (graphdriver), each in plugin and standalone mode.

checks.statement: yes - Docker CLI plugin `docker compose` (cmd/main.go:37-79, plugin.Run with metadata Vendor 'Docker Inc.') and standalone `docker-compose` (cmd/main.go:81-86; flag translation in cmd/compatibility/convert.go:55-108); CI tests both modes (ci.yml:176-191). 35 documented subcommands (docs/reference/compose.md:11-49) plus hidden `alpha` and `hooks` (cmd/compose/alpha.go:26; cmd/compose/hooks.go:164). Machine-readable output: `--progress json` (cmd/compose/compose.go:722-725, 769-775) and `version --format json` (cmd/compose/version.go:64-66).

checks.note: main.go:38 calls plugin.Run, and :72-76 sets metadata.Metadata{Vendor: "Docker Inc."}. main.go:82-83 handles standalone mode: when plugin.RunningStandalone() is true, it rewrites args with compatibility.Convert (convert.go:55-108). ci.yml:176-191 has both mode: plugin and mode: standalone entries. compose.md has 35 table rows at :15-49. alpha.go:26 and hooks.go:164 are both 'Hidden: true'. alpha is registered in RootCommand (compose.go:549), and hooks is added at main.go:47. compose.go:722-725 selects display.JSON for ModeJSON, and :769-775 lists json among the progress modes. version.go:64-66 prints {"version":...} for --format json.

checks.statement: You can create and start your application with a single command, `docker compose up` (README.md:23-24). verified: yes. Evidence: up ensures images (build/pull), models, networks, volumes, then reconciles and executes a plan, then starts services, with depends_on ordering; requires a reachable Docker Engine.
checks.note: README.md:23-24 contains the quoted sentence. In pkg/compose/create.go, :83 is ensureImagesExists, :88 ensureModels, :93-103 networks and volumes, :111 collectObservedState, :127 reconcile and :136 executePlan. pkg/compose/up.go:46 calls s.create, then :51 calls s.start; when attaching, startup happens in runInteractiveUp at :66. cmd/compose/up.go:113-147 is upCommand, which leads to runUp, and :254-270 assembles BuildOptions unless --no-build is set. service_containers.go:162-195 is waitDependencies, and :200-222 polls each depends_on condition (running_or_healthy, service_healthy, service_completed_successfully). The 'yes' verdict holds.
